levels.title: World Religions in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can name the world's major religious traditions and the few things nearly all of them share: beliefs, practices, community and sacred stories.

levels.title: What Counts as a Religion?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why scholars struggle to define religion, comparing a definition by belief in spiritual beings with one by what religion does for a community.

levels.title: Seven Dimensions of Religion
levels.objective: After this level you can use Ninian Smart's seven dimensions (ritual, story, doctrine, ethics, community, experience, material) to describe any religion beyond its beliefs.

levels.title: Studying Religion Fairly
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how scholars describe what believers hold without judging whether it is true, and why no faith speaks with a single voice.

levels.title: The Oldest Signs of Belief
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what ancient burials with grave goods and the stone pillars of Göbekli Tepe suggest about religion before writing.

levels.title: Scripture and Oral Tradition
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what makes a text sacred to a community and how some traditions passed scripture down by memory for centuries.

levels.title: Rites of Passage
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the three stages scholars see in rites of passage, from coming-of-age ceremonies to funerals.

levels.title: Families of Faith
levels.objective: After this level you can sort the world's religions into the Abrahamic, Indian, East Asian and Indigenous families and say what links each family.

levels.title: Counting the World's Believers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how researchers count religious groups, and roughly how large the biggest groups and the religiously unaffiliated are.

levels.title: Checkpoint: What Religion Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how scholars define, study and count religions without taking sides.

levels.title: Abraham and the Covenant
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the covenant Jews believe God made with Abraham, and why Judaism, Christianity and Islam all honor him.

levels.title: Moses, Exodus and Sinai
levels.objective: After this level you can retell the Exodus as Jews tell it, explain the giving of the Torah at Sinai, and say what historians can and cannot confirm.

levels.title: The Hebrew Bible
levels.objective: After this level you can name the three parts of the Tanakh and explain how the Torah is read aloud in the synagogue through the year.

levels.title: Temple, Exile and Return
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple in 586 BCE and again in 70 CE reshaped Jewish life.

levels.title: From Temple to Rabbis
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how rabbis, synagogues and the Talmud let Judaism thrive without a Temple, in a worldwide diaspora.

levels.title: Shabbat
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how and why many Jews keep a weekly day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday night.

levels.title: The Jewish Year
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the meaning and customs of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Passover, Sukkot and Hanukkah.

levels.title: Kosher and the Commandments
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the mitzvot, the commandments Jews follow, using the basic rules of keeping kosher as the example.

levels.title: Branches of Judaism Today
levels.objective: After this level you can compare Orthodox, Conservative and Reform Judaism, and tell these branches apart from Ashkenazi and Sephardi heritage.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Judaism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Jewish belief, scripture, law and practice fit together, from Abraham to Jewish life today.

levels.title: Jesus of Nazareth
levels.objective: After this level you can separate what historians generally accept about Jesus, a Jewish teacher from Galilee, from what Christians believe about him.

levels.title: The New Testament
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Gospels and Paul's letters are and how the New Testament canon took shape over about three centuries.

levels.title: The Trinity and the Creeds
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Christian belief in one God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and how the Nicene Creed set it out.

levels.title: Baptism and Communion
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Christians practice baptism and Communion and why churches understand them differently.

levels.title: Christmas, Lent and Easter
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the shape of the Christian year and why the date of Easter moves from year to year.

levels.title: The Catholic Church
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Catholic Church is organized under the pope and bishops, and what its seven sacraments are.

levels.title: Eastern Orthodoxy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what sets Orthodox Christianity apart, from its self-governing churches to icons and its own date for Easter.

levels.title: The Protestant Reformation
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Martin Luther's protest in 1517 split Western Christianity and what "scripture alone" and "faith alone" mean.

levels.title: Christianity Goes Global
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Christianity's center of gravity shifted to Africa, Latin America and Asia, and why Pentecostal churches grew so fast.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Christianity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Christians believe, how they worship and why they divided into Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant churches.

levels.title: Muhammad and the Revelation
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Muslims believe about Muhammad and the revelation that began in 610, and why the hijra of 622 starts the Islamic calendar.

levels.title: The Quran
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Quran is organized into suras and why Muslims treat its recitation in Arabic as central.

levels.title: One God and Six Beliefs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain tawhid, the oneness of God, and the six articles of faith that Muslims hold.

levels.title: The Five Pillars
levels.objective: After this level you can name the Five Pillars of Islam and explain how together they shape a Muslim's day, year and life.

levels.title: Five Daily Prayers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Muslims prepare for and perform salah five times a day facing Mecca, and why Friday prayer is special.

levels.title: Ramadan and the Two Eids
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Muslims fast from dawn to sunset in Ramadan and what Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha celebrate.

levels.title: The Hajj
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the rites of the pilgrimage to Mecca and why every pilgrim wears the same simple white garments.

levels.title: Sunni and Shia
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a dispute over who should lead after Muhammad's death in 632 produced Islam's two main branches.

levels.title: Hadith and Islamic Law
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how scholars build sharia from the Quran and the Prophet's example, and why schools of law reach different rulings.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Islam
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Muslims believe, how they worship and how Islam's branches and law took shape.

levels.title: Hinduism, a Family of Traditions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Hinduism has no single founder, creed or central authority, and where the word "Hindu" comes from.

levels.title: The Vedas and Upanishads
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Vedas are and the Upanishads' teaching that the self (atman) is one with ultimate reality (Brahman).

levels.title: Karma, Rebirth and Moksha
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why belief in karma and rebirth makes release (moksha) the highest goal for many Hindus.

levels.title: One Divine, Many Forms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how many Hindus worship Vishnu, Shiva or the Goddess as forms of one ultimate reality.

levels.title: Three Paths in the Gita
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the paths of action, knowledge and devotion that the Bhagavad Gita teaches.

levels.title: Puja and Darshan
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Hindus worship through puja at home and in temples, and what it means to receive darshan.

levels.title: Diwali, Holi and the Hindu Year
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the stories and customs behind Diwali and Holi, and why their dates follow the moon.

levels.title: Mahavira and Nonviolence
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Jainism took shape around Mahavira and why Jains extend nonviolence (ahimsa) to every living thing.

levels.title: Jain Vows and Many-Sided Truth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the five Jain vows, how monks, nuns and laypeople keep them, and the idea that truth has many sides.

levels.title: Milestone: Two Families of Faith
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the Abrahamic and Indian traditions: one life and a final judgment, or many lives and release from rebirth.

levels.title: The Buddha's Story
levels.objective: After this level you can retell the traditional story of Siddhartha Gautama's awakening and say what historians can confirm about him.

levels.title: The Four Noble Truths
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Buddha's diagnosis of suffering, its cause in craving, and why he taught that it can end.

levels.title: The Middle Way
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the Buddha rejected both luxury and harsh self-denial, and how the Eightfold Path and meditation put the middle way into practice.

levels.title: No Self and Nirvana
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Buddhists teach that nothing is permanent and there is no fixed self, and what nirvana means.

levels.title: Monks, Nuns and Laypeople
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Three Jewels and why monastics and lay Buddhists depend on each other, from the alms round to Vesak.

levels.title: Three Schools of Buddhism
levels.objective: After this level you can compare Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism, why they differ and where each is practiced.

levels.title: Guru Nanak and the Ten Gurus
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Guru Nanak's message of one God and equality began a new faith in Punjab around 1500.

levels.title: The Guru Granth Sahib
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Sikhs treat their scripture as a living Guru, and what happens in a gurdwara.

levels.title: The Khalsa and the Five Ks
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 and what the Five Ks mean to Sikhs who wear them.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Buddhism and Sikhism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the core teachings, practices and branches of Buddhism and Sikhism and why each began.

levels.title: Honoring the Ancestors
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Chinese ancestor veneration and why families sweep graves at the Qingming festival.

levels.title: Confucian Ritual and Family
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Confucian rites and filial piety, and why scholars disagree over whether Confucianism is a religion.

levels.title: Daoism as a Religion
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Daoist temples, priests and rituals, and the Daoist aims of harmony with the Dao and long life.

levels.title: Buddhism Comes to China
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Buddhism changed in China into Chan (Zen) and Pure Land, and how the "three teachings" came to share one household.

levels.title: Shinto and the Kami
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what kami are and how a Shinto shrine marks off sacred space.

levels.title: Purity, Festivals and Two Faiths
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Shinto purification and festivals, and why many Japanese take part in both Shinto and Buddhist rites.

levels.title: Native American Traditions
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what many Native American traditions share and why each nation's sacred ways belong to that nation.

levels.title: The Dreaming and Country
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Dreaming means for Aboriginal Australians and why land (Country) is sacred.

levels.title: Yoruba Religion and the Orisha
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Yoruba tradition links a supreme God, the orisha and the ancestors, and what Ifa divination is.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Ancestors, Kami and the Land
levels.objective: After this level you can connect ancestors, kami and sacred land into a picture of traditions that live through ritual and place more than creed.

levels.title: The Baha'i Faith
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the Baha'i teachings of the oneness of God, religion and humanity, and the faith's beginnings in 1800s Iran.

levels.title: African Faiths in the Americas
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Vodou, Santería and Candomblé grew from West African traditions among enslaved people and their descendants.

levels.title: Rastafari
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Rastafari began in 1930s Jamaica and what Rastas believe and practice.

levels.title: Church and State in America
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the First Amendment's two religion clauses and where the idea of a "wall of separation" came from.

levels.title: The Great Awakenings
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how revivals in the 1700s and 1800s reshaped American religion and grew the Baptists and Methodists.

levels.title: The Latter-day Saints
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the origins and core beliefs of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and its trek to Utah.

levels.title: Adventists, Witnesses, Pentecostals
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Seventh-day Adventists, Jehovah's Witnesses and Pentecostals began in America and what sets each apart.

levels.title: Faith in Black America
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why independent Black churches and Black Muslim movements became pillars of Black American life.

levels.title: A Nation of Many Faiths
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how immigration since 1965 widened American religion, and what surveys show about Americans' faith today.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Newer Faiths and America
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how new faiths arise and how America's religious freedom shaped its many churches and communities.

levels.title: Religious Law and State Law
levels.objective: After this level you can compare how Jewish law, church law and sharia work, and how religious law has shaped or sits beside the laws of modern states.

levels.title: Why Holy Days Move
levels.objective: After this level you can explain lunar, solar and lunisolar calendars, and use them to predict why Ramadan, Passover, Easter and Diwali move.

levels.title: Food Rules Across Faiths
levels.objective: After this level you can compare kosher, halal, Hindu, Jain and Buddhist food rules and the reasons each tradition gives for them.

levels.title: Why Some Faiths Avoid Images
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Judaism and Islam avoid images of God, and why Christians once fought over icons.

levels.title: Giving as a Duty
levels.objective: After this level you can compare zakat, tzedakah, Christian charity, Buddhist dana and the Sikh langar, and why each faith asks believers to give.

levels.title: Caste and Its Challengers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how caste shaped South Asian society and how Buddhists, Sikhs, devotional poets and B. R. Ambedkar challenged it.

levels.title: Faith and Nonviolent Protest
levels.objective: After this level you can trace nonviolent protest from Jain and Hindu ahimsa through Gandhi to Martin Luther King Jr.'s Christian faith.

levels.title: Persecution and the Right to Believe
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how religious persecution, above all the Holocaust, led the world to declare freedom of religion a human right in 1948.

levels.title: Religion and Science
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why historians reject the story of an endless war between science and religion, using Galileo, Darwin and Lemaître.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Religion Shapes the World
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how religions have shaped law, calendars, food, art, giving, protest and science across the world.

levels.title: Three Kinds of Secular State
levels.objective: After this level you can compare America's separation of church and state, France's laïcité and India's secularism, and weigh what each protects.

levels.title: Atheists, Agnostics, Humanists
levels.objective: After this level you can tell atheism, agnosticism and secular humanism apart and explain their long history.

levels.title: The Rise of the Nones
levels.objective: After this level you can explain who the religiously unaffiliated are and why "none" rarely means no belief at all.

levels.title: Is Religion Fading?
levels.objective: After this level you can weigh the secularization thesis against evidence that the world's population is becoming more religious, not less.

levels.title: Does Religion Cause War?
levels.objective: After this level you can weigh the explanations scholars give for conflicts called religious, separating faith from land, power and identity.

levels.title: Mystics: One Path or Many?
levels.objective: After this level you can compare Sufi, Kabbalist, Christian and Zen mystics and weigh whether mystical experience is the same everywhere.

levels.title: Cult or New Religion?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why scholars prefer "new religious movement" to "cult" and how to judge claims about any group by its actions.

levels.title: Interfaith Dialogue
levels.objective: After this level you can describe interfaith milestones from Chicago's 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions onward, and what dialogue does and does not try to do.

levels.title: Myths About World Religions
levels.objective: After this level you can correct common misconceptions, like the idea that most Muslims are Arabs, using what you know about each tradition.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: World Religions
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of World Religions Levels 1 to 99 across the whole tree.
